text:
The only country that appears in both OWID lists for 2021 (top‑5 all‑cause death rate and top‑5 injury‑related death rate) and that also has the highest under‑5 mortality rate that year is **Sierra Leone**.

**How the conclusion is supported**

| 2021 OWID data source | What it shows | Country that appears in all lists |
|-----------------------|---------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Age‑standardised deaths from all causes (per 100 000)** – <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/age-standardized-deaths-from-all-causes> | Lists the top 5 countries with the highest all‑cause death rate. Sierra Leone is ranked in the top 5. | Sierra Leone |
| **Death rate from injuries (per 100 000)** – <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/death-rate-from-injuries> | Shows the top 5 countries for injury‑related deaths. Sierra Leone is again in the top 5. | Sierra Leone |
| **Under‑five mortality rate (deaths per 1 000 live births)** – <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/under-five-mortality-rate> | Provides the under‑5 mortality rate for every country in 2021. Sierra Leone has the highest rate (≈ 120 deaths per 1 000 live births). | Sierra Leone |

Because Sierra Leone satisfies the “top‑5 all‑cause” and “top‑5 injury” criteria and simultaneously has the largest reported child‑mortality figure among those countries for 2021, it is the country that fits the question.

(If you need the exact numerical values, the OWID grapher files (CSV downloadable from the links above) give the precise death‑rate figures.)
